messages:
Lina: noticed an oddity in the async client for tool/function calls. If I pass return_type=MyDataclass I sometimes get back a raw JSON string instead of the dataclass instance. Happens reliably in our sample app.

Lina: small snippet:```py
@dataclass
class Item:
    sku: str
    qty: int

item = await client.tool_call('fetch_item', input={'sku':'X1'}, return_type=Item)
print(type(item))  # sometimes <class 'str'>
```

diego: Which package version? Any middleware that transforms responses?

Lina: redwood-py 0.9.6 (pulled from our onboarding image). No custom middleware; just using default async client in FastAPI sample. Sync client (sync_tool_call) returns Item correctly.

Priya: can reproduce on my machine. It looks like the async http layer sometimes does resp.text() and hands a string to the serializer which then does json.loads again. If the serializer expects a dict it ends up json.loads('...') working but then we don't convert into dataclass.

QA-bot: Repro steps uploaded: https://ci.internal/artifacts/bug-repro-1860012345.log

Priya: I inspected the code. Two potential root causes: (1) async client wrapper changed to return already-decoded JSON in some codepaths, (2) serializer._deserialize assumes a str. Quick fix: make _deserialize accept both dict and str; if dict, skip json.loads. Add tests for dataclass + pydantic.BaseModel + explicit string payload (tool intentionally returns JSON string).

Lina: Important: onboarding sample app uses dataclasses heavily. This blocked a new trial customer yesterday. We should prioritize a patch.

diego: Agreed. Low-risk fix: in serializers.py, do if isinstance(body, dict): data = body elif isinstance(body, str): data = json.loads(body) else: data = json.loads(body.decode())  # fallback. Add unit tests for async and sync.

Priya: I'll draft a PR that includes tests: tests/test_async_tool_return_types.py covering dataclass, pydantic, and string-return cases. Also add a tiny docs snippet for devex/async_tooling_quickstart.md showing correct async usage with dataclasses.

Lina: Can we also add a small lint rule or CI check to guarantee parity between sync and async tool_call behavior? A smoke test in pipeline would catch regressions.

diego: Good idea. Add a smoke test that runs a minimal async and sync tool_call in CI matrix. I'll open a follow-up ticket for infra.

QA-bot: New failing test on main: tests/test_toolcall_async_dataclass_failure (1 run)

Priya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/4502 - fix + tests + docs snippet. Marked for patch release.

docs-bot: Docs change preview available at https://docs-preview.redwood.internal/1860012345/async_tooling_quickstart.html

diego: CI green on PR, tests pass locally. Merging to patch branch and backporting to release-0.9.x.

Lina: Thanks. Once docs deploy and onboarding sample updated, can we circle back and add a note in the internal cookbook about the pattern to use with dataclasses vs pydantic? Saved us time today.

Priya: Will add a short cookbook snippet after docs go live. Closing ticket after docs deploy.

Lina: great, thx everyone :heart:
